previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, chronic abdominal pain, depression, and recurrent UTIs was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. She also reported pleuritic chest pain and lightheadedness. Workup showed no acute abdominal or renal pathology on imaging, and labs indicated elevated white count without fever or infection signs, consistent with her chronic baseline. Her symptoms were attributed to a gastroparesis flare, worsened by constipation. Supportive care with anti-nausea medication, bowel regimen optimization, and dietary advancement led to improvement. Orthostatic hypotension was linked to antihypertensive medications, particularly propranolol, which was discontinued along with other blood pressure drugs, resulting in resolution of dizziness. Antibiotics were withheld due to lack of infection evidence and concern for resistance. She stabilized on her home insulin regimen, and discharge was planned with follow-up for medication reevaluation and mental health support.
